thread.title: Tech stocks sink under weight of Facebook, chip makers - MarketWatch

author: Wallace Witkowski
title: Tech stocks sink under weight of Facebook, chip makers - MarketWatch
text:
Tech stocks dragged on the broader market Monday as shares of Facebook Inc. tanked following a data-mining scandal that involved millions who use the social media site.
Need to know: Why the case for betting against Facebook is ‘building fast’
Facebook FB, -6.93% shares were suffering their worst day in more than five years as the social network came under fire for improperly managing user information when it revealed that a company with ties to the 2016 Trump campaign improperly kept data on an estimated 51.3 million Facebook users for years when it had been required to destroy the data. Facebook claims to have more than 2 billion active users.
The tech sector was the worst performing of the S&P 500 index’s SPX, -1.66% 11 sectors Monday. The tech sector, which accounts for $6.931 trillion in market capitalization, or 28% of the S&P 500’s total market cap, fell 2.5%, its worst one-day percentage drop since Feb. 8. In comparison, the S&P 500 index was down 1.9% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -2.13% was down 2.5%.
See also: U.S. stocks sink as Facebook’s troubles inspire tech-sector tumble
Other social media shares also were damaged, with Twitter Inc. TWTR, -1.90% down 1.6% and Snap Inc. SNAP, -3.67% falling 4%.
Read: Twitter and Snap are running up big gains in 2018, while Facebook is lagging
Of the largest cap tech companies, shares of Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.69% fell 2.2%, and shares of Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -3.59% GOOGL, -3.53% were down about 3.5%.
Chip makers and chip-equipment providers were hit especially hard across the board with the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX, -2.31% down 2.7%, its worst day since Feb. 8. In addition to supplying datacenters and the promise of AI, the chip sector has also outperformed because of the future of self-driving cars, which make heavy use of advanced computer technology.
On Monday, a female pedestrian was struck and killed in Tempe, Ariz. by an Uber Technologies Inc. self-driving car, believed to be the first known fatality of a pedestrian from a self-driving vehicle .
Nvidia Corp. NVDA, -4.58% shares dropped 5.2%; the chip maker has a deal to provide Uber’s “robotaxis” with self-driving hardware . Advanced Micro Devices Inc. AMD, -0.65% shares were relatively unscathed, only down 0.7%. Shares of Broadcom Ltd. AVGO, -4.14% fell 4.5%, and Qualcomm Inc. QCOM, -4.09% shares shed 4.3%. KLA-Tencor Corp. KLAC, -4.36% shares fell 5.6% after the chip-equipment company agreed to acquire Orbotech Ltd. ORBK, +6.73% for more than $3 billion.
